title: Jade-Juicy Thai Oxtail Kanom Ko
description: A buttery, molten Thai dish featuring oxtail and pound it in a mortar-pestle, inspired from Buddhist temple recipes to enjoy as a comforting dinner. Its rich flavors will make you feel like you're on a sick day, but still wanting more.

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.notes: use fish sauce with a good umami taste

instructions: Pound oxtail with a mortar-pestle until it is tender and easy to shred.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sliced shallots and cook until browned, about 2 minutes.
Add the crushed galangal, kaffir lime leaves, chili peppers, and toasted rice to the pan and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant.
Add the water to the pan and bring to a boil.
Add the oxtail to the pan and cook until it is tender, about 20 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce, sugar, palm sugar, black pepper, and salt to the pan. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded oxtail back to the pan and stir to combine.
Transfer the oxtail mixture to a serving dish and garnish with chopped cilantro, a sprinkle of toasted rice, and a squeeze of lime juice.
Serve the Jade-Juicy Thai Oxtail Kanom Ko hot, garnished with a lime wedge.
This dish is best served with steamed jasmine rice or roti, and a side of spicy chili sauce.
To make this dish more authentic, use a traditional mortar-pestle to pound the oxtail, and adjust the seasoning to taste.
This dish is a variation of a classic Thai recipe and can be adjusted to suit your taste preferences.
Feel free to customize the amount of chili peppers and galangal to your desired level of spiciness.
